extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and readers interested in Mochizuki's IUTT, arithmetic/anabelian geometers, and those following the abc proof controversy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for producing or evaluating expository lectures/manuscripts about Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUTT) and related claimed proofs (e.g., abc). Focuses on clarity, terminology, transparency about claims, and pedagogical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard terminology / avoid neologisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives a statement of the conjecture using completely standard terminology, or at worst nonce words (like “Mochizuki measure space”), the intended meaning of which is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain concepts in standard mathematical terms whenever possible; if inventing temporary/nonce terms, make their intended meaning explicit so readers/listeners can follow without being distracted by unusual verbiage or neologisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract serious ordinary mathematical content
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage to extract serious ordinary mathematical content from Mochizuki’s work and explain what is going on without the verbiage and neologisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the underlying mathematics that can be formulated and checked by experts in standard frameworks, separating substantive mathematical constructions from stylistic or idiosyncratic presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about whether a presentation settles truth or touches on the proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The video doesn’t settle whether it is true or not, or even touch on the proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting material related to contested proofs, explicitly state whether the goal is exposition, formulation, partial derivation, or a verification of the proof; avoid implying that an exposition equals a resolution of correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide errata and correct mistaken explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t forget to check the video description on YouTube for the errata, where in the heat of the moment something was wrongly described/explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and publish errata for recorded talks or drafts; correct mistakes publicly and link corrections prominently so viewers/readers do not propagate errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claiming major proofs are valid without full verification
rubrics_metrics.description: He is not claiming the abc conjecture proof is true; we are still all in the dark as to whether the claimed proof of the abc conjecture is solid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about asserting correctness of sweeping claims (like proofs of abc) until the community has verified all steps; explicitly distinguish exposition of claimed results from endorsement of their validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive intermediate, independently-interesting results
rubrics_metrics.description: We are hoping to make our manuscript deriving some things intermediate to IUT3 Cor 3.12 and IUT4 Thm 1.10 in the next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on extracting and publishing intermediate theorems or computations that have mathematical value independent of the full contested claim; these make progress assessable even if the main claim remains unsettled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and highlight specific concerning steps
rubrics_metrics.description: There are still explicit concerns around one specific step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parts of an argument are suspect, point them out clearly and explain why they are problematic; flagging specific steps enables targeted scrutiny rather than blanket acceptance or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make material assessable by experts with appropriate background
rubrics_metrics.description: People with a solid background of anabelian/arithmetic geometry can start to assess the arguments properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present definitions, prerequisites, and reformulations in standard language so domain experts can follow and evaluate the correctness of arguments; avoid obscure presentation that blocks expert assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible mentorship regarding student involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: I think it’s really irresponsible to have a grad student working on this; a graduate student is better-served by learning some interesting, correct mathematics and working on a concrete, solvable problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the pedagogical appropriateness of assigning contested or highly speculative material as a thesis topic; weigh the risks and benefits for students and provide clearer, safer learning goals when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge controversy and cite critical perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recall that Corollary 3.12 is the point that Peter Scholze and Jakob Stix complained about (not to mention a bunch of other mathematicians, according to Brian Conrad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing contested work, summarize the major criticisms and name relevant critics so readers understand the state of debate; situate exposition within the larger context of expert disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize expository material with prerequisites and modular topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The first videos are going to be as follows: 4 videos on initial theta data, 5 videos on the p-adic logarithm (including Mochizuki's log-links and log-shells), 5 videos on Ind3 and the log-kummer correspondence…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure learning resources into prerequisite modules and focused topic series (prerequisites, key constructions, correspondences) so learners can build up the background needed to assess advanced claims.
